Summary: [EPIC-P1-CONTRACTS] Core contracts v0.9 and Foundry suites (Router v1 without conversion code; mandate lineage; dual caps)
Description:
Core contracts v0.9 and Foundry suites (Router v1 without conversion code; mandate lineage; dual caps)

Phase: P1 | Version: v1.0 | Profile: protocol
Owner squad: Protocol and Contracts | Estimate: 126 person-weeks (108 -> 101 -> 110 -> 126)
Dependencies: RG-016 (protocol freeze); EPIC-P0-PROTOSPEC; EPIC-P0-PROTO
Risk: H: logic bug (RISK-001)

Acceptance criteria: Every invariant in 06 section 4.1 has an invariant or property test; the invariant suite runs at least 1,000,000 calls with zero violations; branch coverage at least 95% on core contracts; static analysis has no unresolved high findings; the absence checks of 09 section 7 pass (no conversion selectors, call targets within the allowlist, no tx.origin); the quote digest and type hashes equal the vector of document 11; role-matrix and fee-ceiling tests pass. Account pin: `consume` reverts `AccountCodeChanged` unless PIN_OK holds, and `updateAccountPin` needs customer authority and never changes a cap. `activateSuccessor` implements exactly the predicates of 12 §5.3, computes the migration snapshot on chain, requires `widenedMask` to equal the computed mask (zero for a migration) and emits the snapshot hash. Lineage, mandate and cycle identifiers contain no router address. `PriceQuote` v1 has the fifteen fields of 11 §4 and checks Q1…Q20; the non-override properties of 11 §4.8 hold under an adversarial signer. `activateSuccessor` has two modes. NORMAL (router still trusted): the old Permit2 allowance may remain only while a sibling mandate of the same customer still relies on the router, and must be zero or expired for a token once no sibling uses it. EMERGENCY (router disabled, sunset, retired or security-deprecated): every token of every mandate of the customer on that router has an unusable allowance first. An on-chain exposure index counts live mandates per (customer, router, token). The `AccountPin` is the seven-field struct; `consume` checks `EXTCODEHASH` of the account and of the delegate; signature capability is bound to the pin and revoked when the delegate, the implementation, the wallet version or the code hash changes. The quote-signer registry supports an immediate tombstone (a compromised signer has no grace and is never registrable again), honors a retired signer set only for quotes issued before retirement and for at most `QUOTE_SET_GRACE`, and lets the guardian stop a whole set. The Foundry suites exported from the Python models (vectors, fuzz, invariant, mutation, integer width, timestamp boundary, shared allowance) run in CI.
Evidence: Foundry reports; coverage report; absence-check report; vector reproduction

Migration requirements: Storage layouts frozen, interface versioning, deployment-manifest schema with several router versions per chain -- Interface and storage-layout changes are versioned and checked against the frozen files in CI; compatibility with the previous version is stated; no change merges without a version decision. Acceptance Criteria: Every invariant in 06 section 4.1 has an invariant or property test; the invariant suite runs at least 1,000,000 calls with zero violations; branch coverage at least 95% on core contracts; static analysis has no unresolved high findings; the absence checks of 09 section 7 pass (no conversion selectors, call targets within the allowlist, no tx.origin); the quote digest and type hashes equal the vector of document 11; role-matrix and fee-ceiling tests pass. Account pin: `consume` reverts `AccountCodeChanged` unless PIN_OK holds, and `updateAccountPin` needs customer authority and never changes a cap. `activateSuccessor` implements exactly the predicates of 12 §5.3, computes the migration snapshot on chain, requires `widenedMask` to equal the computed mask (zero for a migration) and emits the snapshot hash. Lineage, mandate and cycle identifiers contain no router address. `PriceQuote` v1 has the fifteen fields of 11 §4 and checks Q1…Q20; the non-override properties of 11 §4.8 hold under an adversarial signer. `activateSuccessor` has two modes. NORMAL (router still trusted): the old Permit2 allowance may remain only while a sibling mandate of the same customer still relies on the router, and must be zero or expired for a token once no sibling uses it. EMERGENCY (router disabled, sunset, retired or security-deprecated): every token of every mandate of the customer on that router has an unusable allowance first. An on-chain exposure index counts live mandates per (customer, router, token). The `AccountPin` is the seven-field struct; `consume` checks `EXTCODEHASH` of the account and of the delegate; signature capability is bound to the pin and revoked when the delegate, the implementation, the wallet version or the code hash changes. The quote-signer registry supports an immediate tombstone (a compromised signer has no grace and is never registrable again), honors a retired signer set only for quotes issued before retirement and for at most `QUOTE_SET_GRACE`, and lets the guardian stop a whole set. The Foundry suites exported from the Python models (vectors, fuzz, invariant, mutation, integer width, timestamp boundary, shared allowance) run in CI.
